newsitem.title: USA: Another class action filed vs Centennial.
newsitem.headline: Another class action filed vs Centennial.

text.p: A lawsuit seeking class action status and alleging securities fraud by Centennial Technologies Inc and two of its officers has been filed in a federal court in Massachusetts, the law firm for the plaintiffs said Monday.
Law firm of Barracks, Rodos and Bacine said it filed the lawsuit on behalf of buyers of Centennial stock between August 21, 1996 and February 10, 1997.
The lawsuit charges the defendants with "material misrepresentations in the financial statements and reports issued by the company" during the so-called class period.
The lawsuit seeks damages for investors who bought Centennial stock during the period.
Centennial, a maker of personal computer memory cards, was a high flying stock before it was rocked by revelations that its financial statements may have been falsified.

Centennial later announced it would restate its earnings to show a loss for the past three-and-a-half years rather than a profit, following a statement by its newly installed chief executive that the company would be an "easy turnaround."
The company's former chief executive was fired on February 11 and later arrested and held on suspicion of insider trading and securities fraud.
The company's stock was been delisted from the New York Stock Exchange, effective March 3.
